steps.say: Hollins Cross station has two platforms. Points (where the line splits) send a train into platform 1 or platform 2. In this lesson you set routes yourself. There are no trains yet. Press Next.
A route goes from one signal to the next. You set it with two clicks. First click signal H3. It becomes the entrance, where the route starts, and a blue ring blinks round it.

Now H5 and H7 have blue rings too. They are the exits you can reach from H3: a route always ends at the next signal ahead, or at the edge of your area. Signals further on, or behind you, cannot be exits from H3. Press Next.

Click H5 to set the route from H3 to H5. The points are set for platform 1, the route turns white, and H3 turns green. The short white piece past H5 is the overlap: spare track kept clear in case a train runs a little past a red signal. (If H3 is no longer chosen, click H3 first.)
Now cancel the route. Right-click H3 and choose 'Cancel route H3 to H5'. The white track goes grey and H3 goes back to red.
The lesson has set H3 to H5 again. Now try to set a route from H7 to H9: click H7, then H9.

Refused: the alarm list on the right says why. The overlap of H3 to H5 holds the track and points past H5, and your route needed them the other way. The interlocking (the safety system behind the panel) never lets two routes use the same track. Press Next.

The lesson has cancelled its route. Points can also be moved by hand when no route holds them. Right-click the points HP1 (where the line splits before the platforms) and choose 'Swing HP1 reverse'. Reverse leads to platform 2.
Now set the route from H3 to H7, into platform 2. It uses the points as they lie.
Well done. You can set a route (entrance, then exit), cancel it, and move points. Next lesson: running trains through Hollins Cross. Press Next to finish.
